text_fidelity_a: Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad, Ultralight Self Inflating Camping Pads with Built-in Pump, Thick 4 inch Lightweight Inflatable Sleeping Mat for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Camp Sleep Pad [[VIDEOID:da1735cab448c303be82a6fefb9e543e]] I grabbed this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad because my wife and I enjoy days at the beach where we use a tent to have shade in our hot weather, very sunny state. But that sand is brutally hard to lay on - especially on my middle aged back. So I thought this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad would help. It comes nicely rolled in an easy to carry bag - it was also easy to refold and get back into the same bag - how often does that happen? The material seems decent. It feels a bit thick - so it’ll hold up against usage, but can’t speak to it’s strength against things poking out of the ground, so I’d still be careful - as one usually should. My wife laid on it - I’m recovering from surgery and still a few weeks out from such things - and said it was decent - she’d be fine on it on the beach as we’re planning. She is the one who pumped it up - video included - and for the most part it’s very easy. Close the stopped on the back of the pillow and leave the one on the pump open, then start pumping. It filled fairly fast - you see almost all of her efforts in the video. Then close the stopper on the pump. This was the only thing we had issue with. For my first time just to test - pad empty - I had a hard time getting it closed. It took me several tries and several minutes before I somehow got it in. My wife had the same issue - I cut the video as she grew frustrated and edited out that frustration. It did FINALLY close, exactly as it had for me - and all was well. So that was weird. Overall we are happy with this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad. We do wish closing the stopper was easier, but for now, we deal. In the end we would strongly consider a second one if the need should arise.
text_fidelity_b: Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad, Ultralight Self Inflating Camping Pads with Built-in Pump, Thick 4 inch Lightweight Inflatable Sleeping Mat for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Camp Sleep Pad

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Trailblazer Double Bicycle Trailer We purchased this trailer for our 5 year old son to ride in on family bike rides for the next year or so. We spent a few minutes breaking it down and putting it back together in the store, and it was easy and quick to fold up and to set up again. The quick-release on the wheels is what sold us, made of metal, not plastic like others in this price range. The coupler fit easily on my husband's bike, and the trailer can be swapped to another bike in under a minute if the other bike has a coupler (additional couplers can be purchased, they're universal to the Schwinn/Instep trailers). I like that we can remove the stroller handle completely, we'll put this away for future use. The front wheel can be removed as well, or folded 90 degrees to be out of the way. Plenty of storage for picnic supplies or beach gear behind or under the seat.

The seat is a sling, and our son fits well inside, even with a helmet on and the canopy over him. He's 45" tall, and weighs 45 lbs. His posture isn't upright in the seat, he's kind of slouched down with his knees up in front of him, but he says it's fine and he's happy. We're probably going to add some rigid foam to the underside of the seat so that he might sit up a little better. We had used a different trailer (CoPilot) while on vacation, and the seat was a bit more sturdy, but we were able to find this trailer model locally at half the cost of the copilot. We plan to use this trailer for another year or so until our son is able to keep up on his own 2 wheels a little better. I wouldn't even consider putting two kids in this unit, as the sling seat would cause the children to end up in the middle squished together like in a hammock. I don't think it would be very comfortable for two, although the width of the trailer would accommodate two toddlers easily.

The fabric is rather thin polyester canvas with vinyl windows and nylon mesh screening. The seat belts are 1" webbing, they will work for us, but if you're planning to use this for years to come, you might wish to replace it with something sturdier. We had a problem with one of the buckles not staying latched on the canopy. I replaced the buckle with another one. We plan to use this trailer as a beach buggy when we're on vacation once our son outgrows it, so we aren't concerned with how thin the canvas is. I would have looked for a sturdier fabric if we planned to use this as a coach for our son for more than a year or so.

My son cannot easily undo the canopy from inside the trailer. I leave one bottom corner unsnapped so that he can pull the velcro apart by himself. The vinyl rain window rolls up once the canopy is attached. There's a back window that is mesh, with a roll-up fabric cover. The canopy can be completely removed if you wish, but the child could get sprayed with dirt or gravel coming off the rear bike tire, so be aware if that seems to be a problem. For us, it isn't.

My husband says he can't tell the trailer is there unless he's going up or down a hill. It's easy to push with the stroller handle attached, although the stroller front wheel attachment rattles while using it. I wouldn't recommend trying to use this as a stroller very much. If walking at a fast pace, you would need lift the stroller up and use just the back wheels. It would be fine for going short distances or shopping/browsing, although the width would make it difficult to maneuver in crowds. The frame is sturdy and the wheels are well made, we can find tires to replace these with if they get worn out. The ride is adequate for my son, but this isn't the luxury ride that might be expected on a higher end unit.

I was impressed with Schwinn / Pacific Cycle's customer service. The flag to our trailer was missing when we purchased it, so I called the customer service number in the directions. After a few questions about which model I had purchased, they promptly sent out a replacement.

Overall, this is a decent and safe trailer for occasional use. It's lightweight, tracks well behind the bike, is comfortable enough for short rides and my son loves it. Just don't expect a high-end bike trailer for this price, and you won't be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Trailblazer Double Bicycle Trailer

text_fidelity_a:
Isokinetics Inc. Brand Adjustable Fitness Ball Chair - Metal Frame - 2 Frame Finishes - Exclusive: 60mm (2.5") Wheels - Multiple Ball Color Choices - Adjustable Base and Back Height I get so many compliments on this chair! And I love it!

It is constructed very well. It supports my weight well (230 pounds...working on getting that down) and glides easily. I spent some time not realizing that the ball was not completely inflated, probably in fear that it would explode if I pumped too much more. Definitely follow the instructions for blowing it up - you have to let it sit for the night without 100% capacity - so don't buy this with the intention of using it the same day (this is true of any chair like this!) Don't skip that part! Then, when you finally do blow it up all the way, know that in a month or so you may want to blow it up further. When I refilled it, the ball didn't touch the group (even despite my weight!) and it changed where the back bolster hit me. When the ball was less full, the back bolster would hit me mid-back, which was comfortable but also allowed a lot of slouching, which was the main reason I bought this; to combat workplace slouching. Now the bolster hits me much lower and I am more in tune with my posture and less able to slouch.

In terms of aesthetics, I find that this chair is the best choice to use in a professional setting. Sure, it probably still makes me the "quirky" boss who does weird things like sit on a bouncy ball at work...but it also looks the most refined of all the exercise ball chair choices. I got the black ball and silverish-black metal for the most inconspicuous look as possible.

For a while, sitting in this chair would make me really sweaty in the pant area. But after a while, I got used to it and that stopped happening. Some people sell covers for that reason, but I found that the more used to the chair I got, the less sweaty I became in reaction.

Finally, I combat ADHD, and this chair is a fun way to get some energy out in order to "sit still" for longer periods. I try to make sure no one is watching or bounce discreetly. But it's super fun and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Isokinetics Inc. Brand Adjustable Fitness Ball Chair - Metal Frame - 2 Frame Finishes - Exclusive: 60mm (2.5") Wheels - Multiple Ball Color Choices - Adjustable Base and Back Height

Swagtron High Speed Electric Scooter with 8.5” Cushioned Tires, Cruise Control and 1-Step Portable Folding The scooter I got just flat out didn't work. Assembled it, charged it up as instructed in about three hours, hit the throttle and nothing, didn't budge at all. Swagtron customer service said they've heard of Amazon shipping refurbished scooters as new lately, which I'm guessing happened to me because the "new" scooter has a few scratch marks and gouges down near the joint where the handlebars fold up.

Also the rear disk brake is very stiff and you have to manually push the brake lever back into place or else it drags on the wheel, and the screw that fastens the brake lever to the handlebars was almost impossible to turn, I lost some skin on my fingers and stripped the screwhead getting it into place. Now I have to get it off again and pack the whole thing back up.

Amazon customer service is shipping what they say will be a brand new scooter that works, and they're also sending UPS to pick up the old one for no charge. Hopefully this will get resolved but this is all a real disappointing pain in the neck.

UPDATE: Got the replacement from Amazon in a few days as promised. It definitely seems new, since there's packaging and safety stickers that weren't included with the first one I got. No scratches either. The brake lever went on easily and works well. But best of all it actually works. Pick up the front wheel and hit the throttle and it maxes out at 17.9 MPH with no load. Haven't tried it outside yet because of weather but I have been driving around an indoor garage and it hits over 14 MPH no problem, which feels pretty fast. The light works well, the app connects easily. The battery has dropped by 50% just driving indoors so I doubt the range is as advertised.

LifeStraw Flex Advanced Water Filter with Gravity Bag - Removes Lead, Bacteria, Parasites and Chemicals Blue, 1 gal I live in the Pacific Northwest and love to get out into nature. Often, we'll take along water but end up needing more along the trail. When I was a kid, scooping water out of a stream never made me sick, but now I know better! LifeStraw has been an amazing tool to have on board, even for short day hikes.

It’s a 2-stage filter that provides safe drinking water in any environment. We have built up a small collection of LifeStraw products, some for our hiking trips, and some in our emergency kit.

This new version is a huge step above the standard LifeStraw. While the original LifeStraw filtered out bacteria and parasites, this new LifeStraw Flex multi-use water filter with gravity bag removes bacteria and parasites and also removes microplastics and reduces lead - exceeds the NSF 53 standard - from the National Sanitation Foundation website: Filters are certified to reduce a contaminant with a health effect. Health effects are set in this standard as regulated by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Health Canada. Both standards 42 and 53 cover adsorption/filtration which is a process that occurs when liquid, gas or dissolved/suspended matter adheres to the surface of, or in the pores of, an adsorbent media. Carbon filters are an example of this type of product.

For backpackers, hikers and campers, this is a perfect way to drink right from natural water sources. It’s super compact and easy to pack and carry along. Travelers can take this to filter drinking water in places that have a questionable water supply.

There are four ways to use this. As a one-gallon gravity filter bag, as a personal straw (drink straight from a water source), attached to plastic water bottles and adapts to hydration bladders in a backpack.

From the packaging and a little research I did, here are some of the statistics:
Filter Weight: 2.0 oz / Gravity Bag & Hose Weight: 5.3 ounces (dry)
Filter size 6.4”x1.5”
Gravity Bag Volume: 1 gallon
Microbiological filter pore size: 0.2 micron
Removes 99.999% of bacteria, parasites & microplastics
Carbon fiber capsule Improves taste, reduces heavy metals including lead, chlorine and organic chemicals like pesticides, herbicides, and VOCs
Exceeds US EPA drinking water standards for bacteria and parasites
Exceeds NSF 42 standard for chlorine reduction and NSF 53 standard for reduction of lead and other heavy metals
The hollow fiber membrane lasts for 500 gallons and the replaceable carbon capsule for 100 26.4 gallons

Kit Includes: One LifeStraw Flex filter with carbon capsule, 1 gallon / 3.7-liter gravity bag w/ quick connect hose, and a backwashing syringe

text_fidelity_a:
Takeya Actives Sip Lid, Wide Mouth I am writing this review from the perspective of a Hydro Flask owner. Even though this isn't a Hydro Flask lid, it's Takeya, which is still good quality.

I hate all of the hydroflask brand lids. The twist coffee lids have tendency to failure in my opinion, the screw lids are not great if you like to take sips often, and the straw lids are actually not bad, but sometimes, you just don't want a straw. This lid is a great alternative if you want a simple one-handed open close that's still strong enough that it won't open by accident.

Pros
-easy one handed open
-if you look closely at the pictures there is a textured rubber grip that makes grabbing it from the top a more secure feeling
-the moveable handle is nice
-Many other 3rd party lids are either too tight (hard to open) or too loose (prone to accidental openings and leaks). But this one is perfectly right in the middle. It's easy to open one handed, but still fairly secure to resist accidental openings.

Cons:
Like most of these snap lids, the trade-off is slightly less insulation then the HydroFlask brand lids. When I did a side-by side test with several of my Hydro Flask lids, this Takeya melted ice faster than the hydroflask. This is still not too bad as the water was still cold, just not quite as cold as a stock hydroflask lid

Who this is for: You want a more convenient drinking experience and hate the Hydro Flask brand options. Good for one-handed open/close

Who this isn't for: If you must have long-lasting ice in your container for as much time as possible.
text_fidelity_b: Takeya Actives Sip Lid, Wide Mouth

Unfortunately, the manufacturer does not say how long the battery lasts. I will try to add that information after I do more testing.

For the price, this helmet is pretty nice. I just wish the large was larger.

text_fidelity_a:
Arccos Driver Golf GPS Shot Tracker Just a nice weighless device that you put onto your driver, pair with the app on your smart phone, and that's it, it's ready to go.

The application is easy to use. The Arccos app has the information for a number of courses worldwide. I can't say that they are all accurate, can only say it was very accurate for the course I was golfing on today.
Plus it uses GPS to map exactly where you are.

If you're into fun competition, you can share your information with friends for additional competition.
This is a nice device for monitoring your golf driving stats.
There is a summary screen that shows your smart distance, the number of fairway hits, your smart range, longest drive, and your driver handicap.

I am only a recreational player that can only get out a few times a month. So this is just a fun toy for me. I've never tried any other type of GPS tracking devices for golfing so I can't compare the Arccos sensor to any others that are out on the market.
Best to keep your phone in your pocket when you play. You could lose bluetooth connection if you leave it in your bag.

I guess you can purchase a premium subscription but, I couldn't find any information about it. But then again I didn't do any big time researching because it's not anything I would be interested in.
Would be nice if they sold a set for all the clubs. Would be nice to be able to analyze my entire game instead of just the holes where I use my driver.

I'll enjoy using this as an avid golfer. I'm sure the ones that get out and golf more will get full use of all the features that this device has.
text_fidelity_b: Arccos Driver Golf GPS Shot Tracker

Fairly easy to set up the first time out of the box. I did it by myself.
Lightweight enough for a woman to carry
Large floor space and tall enough for a 6' 2" man to stand up in.

Nice rainfly

Cons:
Impossible directions. You don't need them too much to get set up, but you need some guidance to get the tent down and back in the bag. It took 3 tries to finally get it in there

The zippers are not going to take much use, in fact the whole thing might be good for one season of regular camping and use/abuse.

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack T Series Treadmills My primary concerned based on other reviews was that the motor would be noisy. That depends entirely on the speed. If you want it as a walking treadmill, you will definitely hear your footfalls much louder. You could whisper above the motor, no problem. If you are a casual runner and want to take it to say 6 miles an hour (that's pretty much a 30 minute 5K) it's quiet. You can sort of hear it, but not a lot. If you are a pro athlete and want to take it to 10 miles an hour, first off, respect, and second off, you will hear noise about the equivalent to a car engine on the highway.

The iFit attachment, which I recommend, doesn't come with it. You need to buy it, and the subscription, separately. It enables you to download a series of training programs via WiFi including what may be the world's easiest C25K program. They call it Beginner 5K. It's 4 times a week for 12 weeks. It starts with you casually strolling along on the treadmill for half a mile in 15 minute (think the average walking pace of a senior citizen) but it ends with you running uphill at about 5 miles an hour (at that rate you could finish a 5K in roughly 40 minutes) and there are no sudden transitions. It just creeps up the incline a little, then the speed, and soon the fast pace of the old level is the resting pace of the new, but it feels like a resting pace. You build fitness gradually. The treadmill has some pre-programmed routes and workouts built in, and the site has a great many more. My only complaint is there is no way to preview the list before subscribing, to know if it's worth it. Set up for that was a bit of a pain, more so than I'd expected.

I found the left speaker a little weaker than the right, but that could be an audio trick used by Zombies, Run! Otherwise, the sound system is nice. It plugs in via a standard audio cable, not Blutooth in an era where standard audio cables are going out of fashion. There are adapters if that becomes an issue. There are holders for water and phone, etc, and a nice ledge for an ipad.

I like the cushioning, and it is adjustable. I like how easy it is to fold up. Mind, assemble this where you mean to keep it. You're not going to fold it and stuff it in a closet. It's way too heavy for that. Installation takes two people, especially at the end when you have to hold the bottom unit up to install the hydraulic lift. I needed to check a video for that part.

The off switch is to take the little key off the panel. You can use the reset button on the bottom, if you've set it up to be conveniently accessible, but it takes a lot longer to come back from that. It actually takes longer to come back from that, than from shutting of the surge protector it's plugged into, which makes me think it is doing some sort of reset processing. It definitely needs a surge protected, and I recommend the NordicTrack brand for this, just to be safe.

Overall, I'd say this is a high quality treadmill at a reasonable price.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

text_fidelity_a:
MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking UPADATED AGAIN: I have purchased both the 1 and 2 person tent. Seems like very well quality and lightweight. However, the ONE thing that is bad about BOTH tents is the way the end tie outs are sewn and sealed. The tents BOTH leak at the tie out points. This is due to the way they are sealed. It seams as if the seam seal was applied FIRST and then the tie outs sewn into the fabric. This allows water to come through the stitching and leak into the tent. POOR DESIGN. I have remedied this by using seam sealant on ALL stitch points for the tie outs. So, word of caution for everyone owning and buying these tents. MAKE SURE YOU SEAM SEAL EVERY TIE OUT POINT. Once you do that, this tent should be waterproof.

UPDATE: I set this tent up in my yard to test it for waterproof and durability. We had a rain event that came through. No heavy storms. Just light to medium rain that only lasted 10 or 15 minutes. The tent leaked at both ends where the tie outs are sewn into the fabric. These points are seam sealed, so I do not know why or how it leaked at both points. The water on the floor of the tent was about the size of a quarter.
I have since sprayed all of the fly seams and the tie out points with silicone treatment. When we get another rain storm coming through, I will set it up again for another test to see if the spray will keep the tie out points from leaking.
Also, both sides and the rear of the fly, down at the edge, collect water and allow it to pool up. This is a design flaw. I had the tent as tight as I could get it, without damaging the material. The water pooled up around the bottom edge looked like a small moat, and could lead to large amounts of water to run under the tent. This could soak through the floor and get your sleeping gear wet.
I fixed this issue with some micro tarp clamps and 550 cord. I attached one at each end, and two in the rear, one on each side between the rear stake out point and each corner. So 4 total. When I set the tent up again for another rain test, I will update with pictures.
So far, this tent was NOT the tent that all the hype was about. The ONLY positive thing so far, is that it is a true double wall tent, and that will keep condensation out of the sleeping area.

I have not used this tent yet, only set it up. However, with just having set it up, I can see that I will probably like this tent. But, one thing I would like to have seen with it, is more fabric at the vestibule. When set up by the directions, the edge of the vestibule is quite high off of the ground. This would allow for good ventilation during a summer night, but in a rain storm, I would be afraid of rain being blown in.
I have it set up in the yard, and we have a chance of rain today/tonight, so once I let it get rained on and take it out on a trip, I will update my review.
text_fidelity_b: MIER Lanshan Ultralight Tent 3-Season Backpacking Tent for 1-Person or 2-Person Camping, Trekking, Kayaking, Climbing, Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building Great purchase! Delivered with no damage and all parts accounted for. Assembly instructions were clear and easy to follow. They provided tools that will work but I used own. Easy to assemble, took less than 10 minutes. All the parts fit together easily, and seem very well made.

The base is very heavy when filled with water. It also has suction cups on the bottom that work very well on the smooth concrete surface of my garage. In fact too well. It makes moving it around a challenge, but on the plus side it dies not move at all no matter how hard I punch or kick it. Thinking about removing the suction cups because the base is so heavy when filled with water don't think it will move.

The spring is responsive and can handle some pretty hard hits or kicks without the shaft/bag hitting the floor. It's response time to return upright isn't too bad, just don't expect to rapid speed punch if you're going to really hit hard.

The red bag itself is super dense foam, not a leather covered inflatable bag as I've seen on others. It takes quite a pounding and it feels more natural than hitting a leather covered balloon. I've hit it without gloves no issues, but longer workouts need gloves.

The height is adjustable. I'm about 6ft tall, my son is about 5ft tall, and it easily accommodates our heights. A big plus. It's easy to adjust too, and locks in place very securely and stays locked throughout use.

Overall it is a great product and good value for what you pay. Well made, high quality feel that seems it will take a beating and last. Highly satisfied. Would recommend to a friend or family.

One suggestion: after assembly and initial couple of uses, retighten all the fasteners. Initial use may slightly loosen them. After the retighten they'll stay locked in place. I haven't had any issues with things loosening after the first couple of uses.
text_fidelity_b: Midkawe Punching Bag with Stand for Adults & Kids, Adjustable Height Free Standing Boxing Reflex Bag, Ideal for MMA Reflex Speed Training, Fitness,Punching and Muscle Building

text_fidelity_a:
Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA This is an absolutely fantastic keeper glove with just one nuance with the right thumb fingersave.

The gloves are nice and cool with a mesh that lets the hand breathe on the back. The grip is great even though it is smooth! The palms are solid and feel like a mix of latex and neoprene and seem to breathe so my palms don't get as sweaty as other gloves. The latex is a bit soft and after a half-dozen practices with 4-5x the shots I would have in a game, it hasn't disappointed. However, there are some chunks that are missing. I change gloves nearly every season or two. There is a latex wraparound for the thumb that keeps the grip throughout the throw to my teammates. It's like I am getting an extra yard or two and can put a little spin on the ball if I like.

The hard ball comes in up high like a hornet and it's easy to swat down. I just don't feel the sting like some other, thinner, gloves have. Punching the ball is still possible with the fingersave *but* I rarely punch the ball.

The only thing I dislike is how they have the fingersave build into the thumb. It presses in on the top and side of the nail bed and is uncomfortable. I haven't found a way to push it down 1/2 inch and certainly can't change the angle. The left glove fits like, well, a glove and I barely notice the same thing but still notice it. Instead of a hard edge they might need to change the layout of the fingersave.

Normally I wear an Adidas or Reusch and this may be pushing Reusch out and into my new favorite. If I can figure a way out to warm up and melt the thumb fingersave to put a little curve into it, this would be the perfect glove.

I do not wash my gloves so haven't had any issues with the dye. I will gently wipe down the latex and the back of the glove unless the glove gets muddy. There are some renewal products that bring the tackiness back to the latex but I have not tried them with this glove.
text_fidelity_b: Renegade GK Fury Goalie Gloves with Microbe-Guard (Sizes 6-11, 7 Styles, Level 4) Pro-Tek Fingersaves & 4+3MM Giga Grip | High Performance Pro-Level Goalkeeper Glove | Based in The USA

text_fidelity_a: Epiphany Outdoor Gear Pocket Bellows - Weatherproof Collapsible Fire Bellowing Tool for Starting Fire- an Essential Camping Gear After years of blowing at camp fires through pursed lips and getting a face and eyes and lungs full of smoke, I saw a product demonstrated on a Bush Craft video.  It was only available in Europe...  Then I found this on Amazon.  It is stainless steel so it is not light weight for its (small) size.  Its value is in its function and in its collapsiblity.  From a collapsed state of just under 4 inches, it extends to 19 inches,  The larger (.5 inches, diameter) end is placed in the mouth and the narrow end concentrates  oxygenated air from your lungs to a focused stream at the narrow end. Once an initial spark or flame has begun to produce an ember, combustion can be sped up by directing more air precisely at the ember.  That sure beats watching helplessly while the initial spark fails to catch and fades to nothing.  On a dry day with dry, finely processed wood, this might not be needed...but on a cold, damp day with wood that is a bit damp, this makes all the difference between fire and failure.  At first, this device will be stiff to open and close but a little lubricant will help.  Opened up, the rod is sturdy and should last for a good many fires.

text_fidelity_a:
XGrid XGS9USB 9W Portable Solar Panel and USB/LED Flashlight Kit At first I was really excited to get this product, mainly because the idea of using two solar panels to energize a dying cell phone, netbook, or any other device using solar power appealed to me as a novelty. The set feels well-made, each part (the FLEX USB Regular and XGB3L Battery Pack and flashlight) rubberized for protection and assumedly waterproof as well. The panels can be folded up and put into your backpack like a folder, so it doesn't take up too much room.

In terms of functionality, however, I found that using my much-smaller Duracell Powermat does just as good a job of recharging my cell phone when I'm on a trip as this much larger solar panel (and it doesn't require sunlight, just a day in advance to charge it up before a trip). Moreover, the powermat fits in the palm of my hand.

The main advantage this product has over my Powermat is that it has the capacity to power your tablet and larger PC devices as well. The flashlight is a nice touch, but if I bring a flashlight with me with new batteries installed, it's also unlikely I'd have to use solar power for the flashlight either.

So, unless you plan on reading your Kindle or using your Tablet a lot while camping, or expect to be on a long trip in the wilderness or desert where you are unlikely to find a place to recharge a phone after exhausting several powermat-like devices, I would just throw a couple of powermat devices into my bag. Also, weather is never predictable, so if you happen to have the misfortune of traveling on days where it's cloudy or overcast, you might well find yourself stuck with a dead device. As a result, I'd rather pack several small, fully-charged powermats.

I really wanted to like this product, but I found that I like the idea of it (using solar panels) more than the practicality of using this device. However, please note I am speaking as a camper who rarely goes on a trip longer than a week, and doesn't expect to use my phone or tablet all that much while away.
text_fidelity_b: XGrid XGS9USB 9W Portable Solar Panel and USB/LED Flashlight Kit

As soon as it arrived I put it on my bow, First thing about this sight is the pins are small, they are not very bright and they are very clustered with 7 pins. I had no problem sighting in the first pin, and I was able to set the Retina lock in fairly quick and easy on my own. However after shooting some arrows and looking at all the pins I decided not even to bother trying to set the rest of the yardages, it just didn't feel right. The Level bubble and Retina lock do seem distracting to get the all lined up though the peep sight. Sorry to say this wasn't the slight for me.

BEWARE:
If you shoot 1 pin slider and try to go to multi pins, Don't get a 7 pin, stick with 3 or 5 pin max
If you have been use to brighter pins, this is not going to be a good sight because the pins are very faint.
text_fidelity_b: IQ Bowsight Micro 3 or 5 Pin Compound Bow Archery Sight with Retina Lock Technology - Left and Right Hand

OUOYYO 13PCS Camping Cookware Mess Kit Backpacking Hiking Gear with Camping Stove, Compact Light Camping Accessories Cookware Set - Easy Clean Durable Camping Cookware Set with Stove Pan Pot Bowl I have had a number of camp stoves and I have settled on using these butane toppers for ease of use and portability. The built in pieze ignition is a fantastic idea that saves the fumbling with matches and makes lighting a two handed job rather than three. I'm not sure why they are not built into all of these.

What keeps this from being five stars is that it is just too small for a lot of uses. This allows for amazing packability, but the arms are very small and it will not comfortably support anything bigger than a cup or a well balanced small pot. I definitely would not try to actively cook on it, but I do have a camp kettle that seems to balance well, and as long as you are not trying to stir or flip etcetera, it will work. Note, there is a photograph in the listing showing what looks like a cup on the oven, the cup was photoshopped on and the stove itself is considerably smaller.

The build quality is not great.

Pros:
Super packable
Piezo Built in

Cons:
Very small, think heating a single mug for coffee or oat meal

text_fidelity_a: A2ZCARE Threaded Dumbbell Handles/Adjustable Dumbbell Bar Handles - Fit 1 inch Standard Weight Plate - Weightlifting Accessories - Sold in Pair I bought these when the lockdown started and the gyms closed. It took awhile to get them, but so did everything, then. The grips are nice. A bit thicker than my old handles and the knurling is nice. They shed chrome from the threads (they still are) which get pretty sloppy after a short awhile, the "hilt" part of the grips are slightly angled so the plates don't sit quite square which can get distracting and the rubber o-rings are always popping out of the nuts cause they stick to my plates. I can get 5 (you might fit 6, I added a washer to one side of the plates to make loading and unloading them easier) standard cast iron plates (three10lbs, one 5lb and a 2 1/2lb.) on each side with maybe a couple threads or less left. I bought these because my old handles have  shorter plate bars (I'm not sure they're called this, but as opposed to the grip part, OK?...LOL) and they use the quick clips which aren't that secure when using heavier weights on non-horizonal lifts. For lighter, mostly horizontal lifts, I find myself using my old handles more and more. I have a pair of Shark Grips on my old handles that really work my forearms. They don't fit on these. If you're not in a hurry and you want something nice, I'd recommend Olympic handles (2" hole vs 1" on standard) and weights from someone like Cap with  quick collar. I'm not sure how long before I'm ready to go to a gym again, so I'll probably take my own advice.

text_fidelity_a:
OCOOPA Sand Free Beach Towel Microfiber, Extra Large, Quick Dry, Oversized 71x34 inches, XX Large 82x 57 inches, Super Absorbent, Perfect Beach and Swim Towels for Men, Women This beach "towel" comes rolled up in a carry case that is a little larger than a water bottle holder. This is made in China of 90% polyester and10% polyamide. It should not be washed in water above 30 degrees Celsius (86 degrees Fahrenheit) and should never be put in the dryer, ironed, dry cleaned, or bleached.

The material does not feel like the microfiber dusty clothes I have come to know which is fuzzy and catches a lot of lint. Instead, this towel is super soft and slinky and thin. It is also large as can be seen when I laid it across the foot of my king-sized bed. The material repels sand, which is great. However, this is not super absorbent in my opinion. I do not like drying myself with this at all. It does absorb water some but it does not feel right against the skin as a beach towel. I felt like I was drying myself with a slinky scarf.

Nevertheless, I love the design and functionality of this towel. Unfortunately, once the towel is removed from its carrier, the carrier becomes useless. I tried to put the towel back into its carrier after it was dry and it was impossible. Eventually, the carrier just ripped (see photo).

In summary, I consider this more of a thin beach cloth or mat than a towel. I love that it repels sand, feels great against the skin, is lightweight, and large. I love the idea of a carry case but the case is way too small that it becomes useless. I do love the elastic on the towel which allows me to keep it tightly rolled. However, I would never use this like a beach towel to dry myself off. It can, however, be used a little like a wrap on the lower half of the body or slightly over the shoulders. The current price of $20.89 ($21.99 minus 5%) is a little pricey for this. This gets 3.5 stars from me rounded up to 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: OCOOPA Sand Free Beach Towel Microfiber, Extra Large, Quick Dry, Oversized 71x34 inches, XX Large 82x 57 inches, Super Absorbent, Perfect Beach and Swim Towels for Men, Women

text_fidelity_a:
Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel I received this as a review sample and to be honest do not have any recent experience with air mattresses other than this one. That said, I did use it in my home for a solid week, both with the companion [[ASIN:B00U2VI1A8 Lightspeed Outdoors Foam Topper for Air Mattresses]] and without it. If that sounds odd, it's been a long time since I have slept in my bed. Long story, but I can attest that this is infinitely superior to the sofa on which I normally sleep.

Initially I slept on it for two days without the topper and it was absolutely comfortable. Part of that is I was able to stretch out more than I normally do because of the size. With the topper this is an entirely different piece of bedding. It's vastly more comfortable, but also introduces cleaning challenges. I would say that for occasional guests or short camping the topper merits consideration. For longer term use I am not so sure because the topper needs to be professionally cleaned periodically.

The included pump makes this a snap to fill. Note that you will need to supply four D batteries (I would have preferred eight of the more common AA ones, but that is a personal preference.) Deflating it was relatively easy, and it rolls and stores a lot easier than the topper that is made by the same company. In fact, this is lighter (to me, anyway) and less bulky than the topper, and takes up very little space in my home. It can easily store in the bottom drawer of my chest of drawers, or on a linen closet shelf. For camping this does not add a lot of weight when carrying it and a pack, which is another plus in my opinion.

Overall, this is far more comfortable than I remember old style air mattresses to be, and a lot easier to inflate, deflate and pack.
text_fidelity_b: Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel

Cygolite Metro 850 Lumen USB Rechargeable Bicycle Headlight, Black I've been using this light now for a couple of days so here are some initial thoughts. The light seems very well made. Solid construction with a solid mounting bracket. The charge port seems very well sealed as well. About my only complaint was that the mounting bracket barely fit on my large frame size handlebars. Although it doesn't get in the way of my shifting or brake cables, I can see a configuration where it would. A more adaptable mounting mechanism may be in order to handle a larger number of bike variants.

My initial response was that I wish it had more light modes but after using it on the streets and trails round Boston I've found 2 that I switch between and I'm happy. The "Steady Pulse" works well for traffic notification. I've watched cars very specifically react to the light at a good distance even though I'm angling it down to not blind too many people. I can also see it flicker on reflective paint on signs so I know it's got good distance. I also use the low setting for dark bike baths so I don't blind oncoming bikers/runners. I can also easily angle it to one side or the other as well to get it out of people's faces.

I have worked all positions and found them to be very effective. The older version had a plastic liner on the finger holder. That made it very easy to put the whistle in your mouth and pull your fingers out. That way you can use both hands and arms to give signals while holding the whistle with your teeth. These on the other hand have a rubber liner on the finger holder. It is much more secure and much more difficult to pull off your fingers. That's a plus in some situations, but a negative if you need both hands to signal. I'm sure I'll figure out a way to get my fingers out of the holder when needed, but I think I prefer the plastic versus the rubber.

Top quality as always with Fox. The only whistle I'll ever use!

Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce I really hate being the first and only 4 star review but here goes..

I got mine from RawReform, whom I dearly love, and was pleased to get it very quickly and loved all the goodies that came with it.
I HIGHLY recommend that you watch the DVD on the immune system that came with it - very interesting and well done informationally. Mine also came with a book, "Rebounding For Better Health" which I also recommend reading. This book enlightened me and I learned so much from just reading this very simple book!
I'm also glad I did as I learned the importance of 'bouncing' before you 'jump'; and what great benefit the 'health bounce' has for your body!

I completely concur with the other reviewers on the quality of the Needak and would never advise buying BELOW this quality standard. I have not tried folding it yet, so I cannot comment on the ease of doing so. (Unfolding was easy.)

(I had an entire review written and almost completed when my computer fritzed, so I'm trying to remember all the points I had previously written.)

There were a few reviews in particular that cinched the deal and 'sold' me on getting mine. I had recently been troubled with hip problems that a Chiropractor had made MUCH worse (not ALL chiros, just this one) and was getting concerned about my hip/knee pain. My normal forms of exercise were also making it worse and so I wanted to see how rebounding would help.
Let me tell you that with just a couple minutes here and a couple minutes there of doing the 'health bounce' alone has made remarkable differences in my hip/knee pain (almost gone); noticeable improvements in the 'elimination' area; and giving me deeper, restful sleep and less irritability. AND, I've even noticed a slimmer tummy!
Now, how can this be??!!! I'm only doing a COUPLE minutes here and there!
Yet, the book and the DVD will explain how this form of body movement affects your body at the deepest level - the CELLULAR level!
With that information - with those results - how is it that people aren't STAMPEDING and buying these things faster than Amazon can sell their KINDLES!!??
I think it's just a matter of time, and they will.
I realized I had been in the 'dark' too long to not have known the incredible benefits that rebounding/bouncing does for your health, but not any more!

Now..why the four stars instead of five? Well, four is still good. Even three is good. Because, although it says Soft Bounce, it was harder than I imagined. At this time, bouncing with both feet is uncomfortable for ME. My legs throb and ache. So, I've gotten around that by doing a sort of dance 'Twist'; some Jumping Jack type moves and hops and that seems to do the trick. Am I just more out of shape than I thought? Will it eventually improve? I don't know. I'll let you know.
I can't help but wish that I were able to COMPARE my rebounders bounce/feel with other rebounders of EQUAL or GREATER value in order to see if another would've been more comfortable for me, but I'll not ever have that opportunity to do so; and this was my price range and I am content with it and would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce
